learningObjectives: Create a child Case during Case processing using a Create Case automation Step.
Choose between copying data and using a data reference when propagating data from a parent Case to a child Case.

items: TOP-LEVEL CASE — has NO parent but CAN become one (e.g., Accident Claim)
CHILD CASE — created within a parent Case (e.g., Vehicle Damage, Medical, Rental Car — each handled by different parties)

elements.text: A project can have separate repair and inspection workstreams. Each follows its own plan and reporting needs. In the parallel child-Case model described here, finishing the parent requires the children to finish; this does not mean every intermediate parent Step is blocked. Design the coordination points rather than assuming a universal pause.

elements.description: Use child Cases when work is performed by DIFFERENT PARTIES, follows DIFFERENT REPORTING OPTIONS, operates on DIFFERENT TIME FRAMES, or is COMMON TO MULTIPLE Case Types (reuse).

Configure a Create Case automation in the parent Process to instantiate the intended child Case Type. Creation happens when that Step runs. Additional Dev Studio options include top-level creation and multiple children; the shape is not inherently child-only.

elements.term: Data propagation — Copy vs. Data reference
elements.description: How parent data is shared with child Cases:
items: COPY DATA — propagates selected values at creation; later parent edits do not synchronize the copy automatically. The child copy can still be edited by its own configured work.

DATA REFERENCE — use referenced parent data when later parent updates should remain available; advanced Dev Studio configuration is required. Do not infer a specific data-page implementation or write permission from the relationship alone.

elements.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 190" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Child work and data sharing</title><rect x="10" y="10" width="740" height="170" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="30" y="42" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="var(--pa-brand)">One parent, separate child workstreams</text><g font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)"><text x="30" y="78">Configured Create Case Step → child instance and its own workflow.</text><text x="30" y="110">Copy for a creation snapshot; reference for changing parent information.</text><text x="30" y="142">Parallel-child completion gates parent resolution, not every parent Step.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: Separate child workflows support decomposition and reuse. In the described parallel model, children complete before parent resolution.

examPitfalls.title: Top-level Case has NO parent — but CAN become a parent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates confuse top-level Cases with Cases that can never be parents. A top-level Case starts without a parent but can spawn child Cases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Top-level Case = no parent Case above it, but it CAN create child Cases below it (making it a parent). Child Case = has a parent Case.

examPitfalls.title: Create Case is an AUTOMATION Step — not a Process or manual Step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what type of element creates a child case in the Case Life Cycle. Candidates say 'a Process' or 'a manual Step.' Creating a child case is configured as an Automation Step — specifically the 'Create Case' automation shape in the Case Life Cycle.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure the Create Case automation to create the intended child when the Process reaches that Step. Other creation options exist in Dev Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Copy data = snapshot, NOT synchronized
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether the copied data in a child case updates when the parent case data changes. Candidates say yes. The 'Copy data' option takes a snapshot at child creation time — subsequent changes to the parent are NOT reflected in the child.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A propagated value is not automatically refreshed by later parent edits. This is a copy, not a live link, but it is not an immutable field.

examPitfalls.title: Data reference = synchronized — but requires Dev Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how to keep child case data synchronized with parent data. Candidates say 'use Copy data.' A data reference keeps the child synchronized with the parent, but configuring a data reference requires Dev Studio — it is not available in App Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Data references keep child Case data synchronized with the parent. This requires ADVANCED CONFIGURATION IN DEV STUDIO — it cannot be done from App Studio alone.

examPitfalls.title: Child Cases have their own independent lifecycle
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether the child case follows the parent case's stages. Candidates say yes. Child Cases have a completely independent Case Life Cycle — they can be configured with different stages, processes, and SLAs from the parent.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A child is an instance of its configured Case Type, whose workflow can differ from the parent. Relationship hierarchy does not copy the parent lifecycle.

examPitfalls.title: Case Type reuse is a key benefit of child Cases
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not declare reuse the single primary benefit for every design. Parallel work, specialist ownership, separate reporting and timing can also motivate decomposition.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: An existing child Case Type can serve several parent Case Types. Choose decomposition for the actual work requirements rather than a universal ranking of benefits.

examPitfalls.title: Four specific situations where child Cases are beneficial
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask for valid reasons to use child Cases — candidates confuse them with reasons to use Alternate Stages or optional Processes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Child Cases are for: (1) different parties, (2) different reporting options, (3) different time frames, (4) work common to multiple Case Types. These are distinct from Stage/Process configurations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An auto insurance 'Accident Claim' Case needs separate tracking for vehicle damage (handled by a repair shop) and medical treatment (handled by a clinic). Why is a child Case the right approach?

options.text: Different parties perform different work — child Cases allow each party to have an independent Case lifecycle
The repair shop and clinic must use different applications — child Cases support multi-application workflows
Child Cases are required when a Case has more than two Stages
Child Cases automatically notify external parties without an email Step

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate specialist work can use independent workflows while retaining the parent relationship.

optionExplanations.A: Separate specialist work can use independent workflows while retaining the parent relationship.
optionExplanations.B: This scenario does not require separate applications for the two specialists.
optionExplanations.C: A Stage count does not determine whether work needs a separate Case.
optionExplanations.D: A hierarchy does not by itself configure outbound notifications.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is advising a client on when to decompose a complex Case into parent and child Cases. Which TWO situations are valid business reasons to use child Cases in a Pega application?

options.text: Work that follows different time frames
Work that is common to multiple Case Types (reuse)
Work that requires more than 10 Steps in a single Process
Work that must be hidden from the parent Case owner

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Distinct schedules can justify separately managed child workflows. A reusable Case Type can provide common work for more than one parent design.

optionExplanations.A: Distinct schedules can justify separately managed child workflows.
optionExplanations.B: A reusable Case Type can provide common work for more than one parent design.
optionExplanations.C: An arbitrary Step count is not the business decomposition criterion here.
optionExplanations.D: A child relationship does not by itself restrict the parent owner’s access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does an SA add a child Case to a Case Type in App Studio?

options.text: Add a Create Case Automation Step to the Case Life Cycle
Add a child Case Type in the Stage properties panel
Configure a Case hierarchy in the Case Type settings under the Relationships tab
Create a When Rule that triggers Case creation when conditions are met

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Place and configure the creation automation in the parent workflow for the desired child type.

optionExplanations.A: Place and configure the creation automation in the parent workflow for the desired child type.
optionExplanations.B: A Stage-property entry is not the creation Step requested in this question.
optionExplanations.C: A hierarchy description alone does not instantiate the child at the intended Process point.
optionExplanations.D: A Boolean test alone is not the creation automation; it can express a condition but does not create work by itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is designing a complex insurance application with parent Cases that spawn child Cases for sub-investigations. The developer asks an SA to define what a top-level Case is in relation to this hierarchy. What is a top-level Case in Pega Platform?

options.text: A Case that has no parent Case but can become a parent by creating child Cases
A Case that has no parent and cannot create child Cases
A Case at the top of the Case hierarchy that automatically aggregates all child Case data
A Case Type that serves as a template for all other Case Types in the application

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The term describes the absence of a parent above the current Case, not a prohibition on descendants.

optionExplanations.A: The term describes the absence of a parent above the current Case, not a prohibition on descendants.
optionExplanations.B: Having no parent does not prevent creating children below it.
optionExplanations.C: Hierarchy does not automatically aggregate every child field.
optionExplanations.D: A relationship role is not an application-wide Case Type template.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A child Case should read changing parent address information rather than retain only the creation-time value. Which approach fits this requirement?

options.text: Data reference — keeps the child Case data synchronized with the parent
Copy data — copies the current address at creation and stays current automatically
Data reference — only available in App Studio via the Create Case Step configuration
Copy data — Pega automatically re-copies parent data every time the parent Case is updated

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A reference fits changing parent information; creation-time copying alone cannot meet this need.

optionExplanations.A: A reference fits changing parent information; creation-time copying alone cannot meet this need.
optionExplanations.B: The copy is not automatically refreshed by later parent edits.
optionExplanations.C: This incorrectly locates the advanced reference configuration in App Studio alone.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic copying on every parent update is not inherent in propagation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Only 'Copy data' propagation is configured for a phone number; no later synchronization logic exists. After creation, the parent number changes. What happens to the child copy?

options.text: It remains unchanged — copy data captures a snapshot at creation time only
It updates automatically — copy data creates a live reference to the parent field
It updates the next time the child Case is opened by a user
It triggers a warning that the data is out of sync and prompts the user to refresh

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Without additional synchronization logic, the propagated phone value remains the original copy.

optionExplanations.A: Without additional synchronization logic, the propagated phone value remains the original copy.
optionExplanations.B: Propagation does not turn the copied field into a live reference.
optionExplanations.C: Opening a child does not itself refresh a copied parent value.
optionExplanations.D: No automatic stale-data warning or refresh prompt follows merely from using a copy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA wants to configure a data reference in a child Case so its data stays synchronized with the parent. Where is this advanced configuration performed?

options.text: Dev Studio — data references require advanced configuration not available in App Studio
App Studio — the Create Case Step has a 'Synchronize' toggle for data references
Admin Studio — data synchronization is a system-level setting
The Case Life Cycle's Stage properties panel — select 'Inherit parent data' on the child Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Advanced reference configuration belongs in Dev Studio in this lesson.

optionExplanations.A: Advanced reference configuration belongs in Dev Studio in this lesson.
optionExplanations.B: This invents a Synchronize toggle for the described App Studio creation setup.
optionExplanations.C: A system administration setting is not the documented reference setup.
optionExplanations.D: A child workflow Stage does not provide the proposed Inherit parent data switch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'New Account Onboarding' Case Type needs a 'Background Check' Process that is also used in a 'Job Application' Case Type. What child Case benefit applies?

options.text: Work common to multiple Case Types — the Background Check Case Type can be reused as a child Case in both
Different parties — background checks are performed by external vendors
Different time frames — background checks take longer than onboarding
Different reporting options — background check results require a separate report

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Using one Background Check Case Type in both parent designs illustrates reuse directly.

optionExplanations.A: Using one Background Check Case Type in both parent designs illustrates reuse directly.
optionExplanations.B: External-vendor ownership is not established by the question; it is a separate possible motivation.
optionExplanations.C: The question does not state how long either workflow takes.
optionExplanations.D: A separate reporting requirement is not supplied in this scenario.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Create Case automation is configured to create a child of a specified Case Type. What happens when the parent Process reaches this Step?

options.text: A new child Case of the configured Case Type is created automatically
A user is prompted to confirm whether to create the child Case
The parent Case pauses until the child Case is manually created by a manager
A draft child Case is created but must be submitted before it becomes active

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The configured creation Step instantiates the chosen child; its later workflow can still involve users.

optionExplanations.A: The configured creation Step instantiates the chosen child; its later workflow can still involve users.
optionExplanations.B: This assumes a confirmation assignment that is not part of the described creation automation.
optionExplanations.C: The automation creates the child rather than waiting for a manager to create it manually.
optionExplanations.D: This invents an obligatory draft-submission phase for every created child.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Does a child Case follow the same lifecycle (Stages, Processes, Steps) as its parent Case?

options.text: No — the child instance follows its configured Case Type lifecycle, which can differ from the parent
Yes — the child Case inherits the parent's lifecycle by default
Yes — but only the Stages are inherited; Processes and Steps are independent
No — child Cases have no lifecycle and are completed through manual status updates only

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The child uses its configured workflow, rather than inheriting Stages through the parent relationship.

optionExplanations.A: The child uses its configured workflow, rather than inheriting Stages through the parent relationship.
optionExplanations.B: A parent link does not automatically copy the parent workflow definition.
optionExplanations.C: The relationship does not impose Stage inheritance while leaving only the smaller elements independent.
optionExplanations.D: A child has a workflow; it is not restricted to arbitrary status edits.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which configuration option does Dev Studio provide for the Create Case Step that App Studio does not?

options.text: Additional contextual creation options, including creating a top-level Case or multiple child Cases
Specifying the Case Type for the child Case
Mapping selected parent fields to child fields for copy propagation
Setting the child Case priority level

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dev Studio exposes additional creation options; this describes more than the ordinary selected child creation.

optionExplanations.A: Dev Studio exposes additional creation options; this describes more than the ordinary selected child creation.
optionExplanations.B: Selecting the child type is already part of the described App Studio Step configuration.
optionExplanations.C: App Studio can map copied field values, so this is not the additional Dev Studio capability.
optionExplanations.D: Priority is not the additional creation capability established by this source; the answer does not explain the documented distinction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is choosing between 'copy data' and 'data reference' for a child Case. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Copy data captures a snapshot at creation — it does not update if the parent changes
Data reference keeps child data synchronized with the parent and requires Dev Studio configuration
Copy data automatically re-syncs when the parent Case is submitted
Data references can be configured from App Studio without any Dev Studio involvement

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Copy propagation captures selected creation-time values and does not synchronize later parent changes by itself. Referenced parent information fits ongoing changes and requires advanced configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Copy propagation captures selected creation-time values and does not synchronize later parent changes by itself.
optionExplanations.B: Referenced parent information fits ongoing changes and requires advanced configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Submitting the parent does not inherently refresh a propagated child copy.
optionExplanations.D: This incorrectly removes the advanced Dev Studio work required for the reference.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to propagate customer contact data from a parent Insurance Case to a newly created child Investigation Case. Which TWO statements correctly guide this design decision?

options.text: Copying data creates an independent snapshot in the child Case — changes in one Case do not automatically affect the other
Use referenced parent data when parent updates should remain available to the child; configure the reference in Dev Studio
Copying data from parent to child automatically keeps both records in sync when either record is modified
A data reference in the child always overwrites the parent's data if the child modifies the referenced value

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the relationship, creation configuration and data-sharing behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The copies are separate values; later edits do not inherently synchronize the two Cases. Reference the changing information rather than promising a permanently current copied value.

optionExplanations.A: The copies are separate values; later edits do not inherently synchronize the two Cases.
optionExplanations.B: Reference the changing information rather than promising a permanently current copied value.
optionExplanations.C: This attributes two-way synchronization to a one-time copy operation.
optionExplanations.D: A reference alone does not establish write-back behavior or authority to overwrite the parent.

quickRecap.value: No parent Case, but CAN create child Cases. Child Case = has a parent.
(1) Different parties, (2) different reporting options, (3) different time frames, (4) work common to multiple Case Types.
Configured automation instantiates the intended Case when reached. Dev Studio exposes additional creation options.
Snapshot of parent data at creation time. Does NOT update if parent changes later.
Stays synchronized with parent data. Requires advanced configuration in Dev Studio.
Child instances follow their configured Case Type workflow; a parent relationship does not copy the parent lifecycle.
Implementing work in a separate Case Type allows it to be reused as a child Case across multiple parent Case Types.
